To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a phase-delayed inhibitory circuit is capable of encoding whisker deflection information, and that adaptation of the circuit improves its ability to discriminate between different whisker deflections.

the feedforward circuit of TC cells, inhibitory FS cells, and an RS cell can explain the experimental data and, moreover, that the network structure of the phase-delay inhibition circuit enables RS cells to encode whisker deflection information.

the RS cell spiking response to whisker deflection can be explained by a purely feedforward circuit and that the phase-delayed structure of the network is crucial to the ability of the system to decode TC population synchrony.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the ability of the feedforward network to encode whisker deflection features within the rodent somatosensory cortex, and we show that a purely feedforward circuit can indeed explain the experimental data.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phase-delayed inhibitory circuit structure within the feedforward circuit is a key factor in the ability of the RS cell to decode deflection velocity from TC population synchrony.
the phase-delayed network structure is a key feature that allows the RS cell to decode TC population synchrony, and hence to encode whisker deflection, velocity.
phase-delayed inhibition is a necessary, but insufficient, component of the barrel cortex network structure that enables whisker deflection speed decoding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phase-delayed inhibitory network structure is essential for the ability of RS cell to decode TC synchrony.
the phase-delayed network structure is necessary but not sufficient for the ability of an individual cortical RS cell to decode deflection velocity.

the phase-delayed inhibitory network structure, together with adaptation, is necessary to explain the data, and that the phase-delay structure plays a key role in the ability of an individual RS cell to decode TC synchrony.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the feedforward circuit is capable of explaining the experimental data on the response of RS cells, and that the phase-delayed structure of the network is critical to the ability of RS cells to decode whisker velocity.
the phase-delayed inhibitory network structure is crucial for the decoding of whisker deflection by the RS cell.
phase-delayed inhibition plays an important role in the ability of the barrel cortex to encode whisker deflection.
